source: Store API resource contracts, executed through the hosted connector
credentials: Merchant admin tokens and the merchant’s own MCP connection only; apps may not hold domain/email-settings scopes.
workflow: Read get_email_overview first: badge, the four steps in order (sending domain, sender address, default sender, reply-to), next_action and health.
Follow next_action: call next_action.tool with next_action.arguments after the merchant agrees. Show labels, messages, record status texts and issues as given.

Call verify_email_domain once when the merchant says the records are added. Never call it in a loop: Tringify checks in the background; look again with get_email_domain after next_action.after (or setup.poll_after_ms while verifying).

Removal: check_email_domain_removal or check_email_sender_removal, show confirm and every impacts[].message, then request_verification_code (its next_action) and delete_email_domain or delete_email_sender with otp_code.

step_up.flow: Call request_verification_code with the exact action, target_type and target_id documented by the selected tool (a refused call's details.next_action and a removal check's next_action give them). Tringify emails the code to the connected merchant. Ask the merchant for it and pass it as otp_code. The connected tool cannot invent or bypass this code.

guide: Every store has a Tringify address such as noreply@your-store.mytringify.com. It needs no setup and cannot be removed. Emails come from it until the merchant chooses a default sender, and whenever the chosen sender cannot send. Marketing is never moved to another sender automatically: it pauses until a marketing sender can send.

A sending domain must be, or be under, a domain connected to the store in Settings > Domains, for example mail.example.com under example.com. Its setup steps are always: add the sending domain, add the DNS records, Tringify verifies the records, verified, ready to send.

Each sending domain needs six records: three Tringify email signing (DKIM) CNAME records, two Tringify email bounces records (MX and TXT on bounce.<domain>) and one email policy (DMARC) TXT record. When Tringify hosts the domain's DNS it writes and locks all of them itself. Otherwise the merchant copies each host (relative to the zone) and value; each record shows what public DNS has now.

Missing or invalid DMARC and missing or changed bounce records never stop sending; they are shown as an issue with its fix. Signing records not found within 72 hours stop verification (restart creates new signing records). Signing records that change later, or a base domain no longer connected, stop the domain from sending; emails then come from the Tringify address and the merchant is notified.

Removing a sending domain or sender address shows its impacts first (senders removed, the Tringify address taking over as default sender, marketing paused, DNS records Tringify deletes) and needs a verification code. Removing the default sender is allowed.

Health: bounce rate warning from 2%, critical from 5%; spam complaint rate warning from 0.1%, critical from 0.3%; rates count once the store sent 100 emails in 30 days. Each issue has a cause and a fix.

Reply-To has separate active and pending values. Pending links expire after seven days; resend is available after the server cooldown. Save the active value to cancel the pending request; save the pending value to resend. Clearing the active value removes the Reply-To override. Reply-To applies to merchant transactional and marketing messages; platform notifications use their separate identity.

Email history uses a stable cursor. Calendar date filters use the store timezone. History and totals share type, status and date filters. Sent includes sent, bounced and complained outcomes. Delivered means recipient-server acceptance, not an inbox placement or read receipt. Delivery rate is delivered divided by sent. Do not automatically resend an uncertain message. A spam-complaint suppression cannot be lifted; suppression is different from marketing consent.

Shared sending capacity can delay sending without changing the allowance or sender choice. Marketing includes a visible unsubscribe footer and one-click headers; opening the unsubscribe link alone does not unsubscribe. Transactional and test messages do not use marketing unsubscribe headers.
Installed and third-party apps cannot hold domain or email-settings scopes. Public contact email is a separate storefront field; it is not the owner login, a sender or the Reply-To address.
schema_parity: Run scripts/check-email-catalog.py with an export of the hosted connector's tool catalog and --docs-catalog pointing to the connector docs catalog.
